title: Grove's mandate is an institutional-grade credit platform that moves yield between the traditional and onchain economies
content:
A.6.1.1.2.1 states Grove's purpose in two clauses: it is "an Agent focused on unlocking the full potential of USDS through higher savings rates and new products and opportunities," and its "main focus will be building an institutional-grade credit platform designed to facilitate credit creation and seamlessly move yield in and out of the onchain economy."

The second clause is the load-bearing one because it narrows an open-ended goal into a specific business. Higher savings rates for USDS holders are the *outcome*; credit creation is the *mechanism*. Grove is not chartered to raise yield by any available means — it is chartered to raise it by originating and intermediating credit.

The phrase "in and out of the onchain economy" commits Grove to being a bridge rather than a purely onchain strategy. That implies exposure to off-chain counterparties, legal structures and settlement latency, which is why the rest of the Grove Artifact spends so much of its length on custodial accounts, allocator contracts and role-gated operational processes.

"Institutional-grade" is also a constraint, not just marketing: it commits Grove to the operational and reporting standards that institutional credit counterparties require, which is a cost Grove must bear regardless of whether onchain participants demand it.
description: Grove is a Prime Agent whose stated purpose is unlocking USDS potential through higher savings rates; its chosen instrument is credit creation, not trading or liquidity provision.
